biological.citation: N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea-Induced Adaptor Protein 2 Sigma Subunit 1 (Ap2s1) Mutations Establish Ap2s1 Loss-of-Function Mice (PMID: 29479578)
biological.summary: AP2S1 encodes the AP2σ subunit of the heterotetrameric AP-2 complex (with AP2α, AP2β, and AP2μ), which is pivotal for clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Loss-of-function mutations impair internalization of the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR), causing familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type-3 (FHH3). Homozygous Ap2s1del17/del17 mice were non-viable and died between embryonic days E3.5–E9.5, indicating essential roles during embryonic patterning and organogenesis.

biological.citation: The HAVCR1-centric host factor network drives Zika virus vertical transmission (PMID: 40156834)
biological.summary: A genome-wide CRISPR screen in placental trophoblasts identified AP2S1 as a host factor cooperating with HAVCR1 for Zika virus (ZIKV) internalization through clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Proteomic profiling and functional analyses confirmed that AP2S1 is required for ZIKV entry in placental cells. This highlights AP2S1's role in clathrin-mediated endocytosis as exploited by ZIKV during vertical transmission.

biological.citation: High-Confidence Interactome for RNF41 Built on Multiple Orthogonal Assays (PMID: 29560723)
biological.summary: AP2S1 was identified as a novel interaction partner of RNF41 (an E3 ubiquitin ligase) through a high-confidence interactome built from affinity purification-mass spectrometry, BioID, Virotrap, MAPPIT, and Y2H screens. Functional validation revealed a role for AP2S1 in leptin and LIF receptor signaling. RNF41 was shown to stabilize and relocate AP2S1 within the cell.
biological.sample_size: 175 candidate protein partners identified; 19 in high-confidence set

biological.citation: Proteomics Reveals AP-2 Complex Depletion Suppressing Listeria monocytogenes Intracellular Replication (PMID: 40847839)
biological.summary: L. monocytogenes infection significantly upregulates Ap2s1 expression in host macrophages (Raw264.7), dendritic cells (DC2.4), HeLa, and Caco-2 cells. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of Ap2s1 (along with Ap2m1 and Ap2a2) markedly inhibited intracellular bacterial proliferation. These findings establish AP2S1 as a host factor exploited by L. monocytogenes to promote post-phagosomal cytosolic replication.
biological.sample_size: Multiple cell lines (Raw264.7, DC2.4, HeLa, Caco-2)

biological.citation: GTPase GPN3 facilitates cell proliferation and migration in non-small cell lung cancer by impeding clathrin-mediated endocytosis of EGFR (PMID: 39893205)
biological.summary: AP2S1 was identified as an interaction partner of GPN3 (a GPN-loop GTPase) along with clathrin light chain A (CLTA) and AP2B1, placing AP2S1 within the clathrin-mediated endocytosis machinery. GPN3 upregulation inhibited clathrin-coated pit invagination and reduced EGFR endocytosis, a process in which AP2S1 participates as a modulator. This interaction was identified in the context of non-small cell lung cancer.

biological.citation: Codon Arg15 mutations of the AP2S1 gene: common occurrence in familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia cases negative for calcium-sensing receptor (CASR) mutations (PMID: 24731014)
biological.summary: Recurrent missense mutations at codon Arg15 of AP2S1 (p.R15C, p.R15L, p.R15H) were identified in 5 of 39 (13%) FHH patients lacking CASR mutations, confirming AP2S1 as a cause of FHH type 3. AP2S1 encodes a sigma subunit that interacts with the CaSR and is required for its proper internalization via clathrin-mediated endocytosis. The FHH3 phenotype did not differ materially from FHH1 caused by CASR mutations.

biological.citation: In Vitro Control of Genes Critical for Parathyroid Embryogenesis by Extracellular Calcium (PMID: 32666007)
biological.summary: AP2S1 mRNA expression was assessed in primary cultures of adult parathyroid adenoma tissue under varying extracellular calcium concentrations (0.1–3.0 mM). Unlike CaSR and GNA11, which showed sensitivity to low calcium concentrations, AP2S1 exhibited a variable and less pronounced response to extracellular calcium. This study places AP2S1 within the calcium regulatory signaling pathway expressed in adult parathyroid cells.

biological.citation: Familial Hypocalciuric Hypercalcemia Types 1 and 3 and Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Similarities and Differences (PMID: 26963950)
biological.summary: In a large cohort, three recurrent AP2S1 mutations were identified in 19 families with FHH type 3, establishing AP2S1 loss-of-function as a distinct genetic cause of FHH. Patients with FHH type 3 (AP2S1 mutations) had higher plasma calcium concentrations and higher renal tubular calcium reabsorption than FHH type 1 (CASR mutations), despite similar PTH levels. This indicates that AP2S1 mutations affect calcium homeostasis more severely than CASR mutations.
biological.sample_size: 22 FHH type 3 patients, 52 FHH type 1 patients, 60 PHPT patients

biological.citation: Proteomic analysis of boar sperm with differential ability of liquid preservation at 17 °C (PMID: 38029685)
biological.summary: Quantitative proteomics (TMT labeling) of boar sperm identified AP2S1 as one of 8 candidate biomarker proteins differentially expressed between sperm with good versus poor liquid preservation ability. AP2S1 was identified through protein-protein interaction network analysis as a hub protein among 187 differentially expressed proteins. This suggests AP2S1 protein is present and functionally relevant in boar sperm.

biological.citation: Analysis of AP2S1, a calcium-sensing receptor regulator, in familial and sporadic isolated hypoparathyroidism (PMID: 24423332)
biological.summary: Sequencing and quantitative genomic PCR of AP2S1 in 60 patients (10 familial, 50 sporadic) with isolated hypoparathyroidism found no nucleotide changes or copy number variations, excluding AP2S1 defects as a frequent cause of hypoparathyroidism. This study characterizes AP2S1 as a calcium-sensing receptor regulator whose gain-of-function (not loss-of-function) is associated with hypercalcemic rather than hypocalcemic phenotypes. The negative result clarifies the directional specificity of AP2S1 mutations in calcium disorders.
